# Link accessibility conformance

Rated against WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA. See the [reports legend](../accessibility.md).

| Result                | Count |
| :-------------------- | :---- |
| ✅ Supports           | 22    |
| ⚠️ Partially Supports | 2     |
| ❌ Does Not Support   | 0     |
| ➖ Not Applicable     | 31    |
| 🚩 Flagged            | 6/24  |

## Known gaps

- ⚠️ **1.4.1 Use of Color.** <!-- 1.4.1:gap:start -->The default `underline="always"` passes. With `underline="none"`, a link in body text relies on color. With `underline="hover"`, `secondary`, `textSecondary`, `textPrimary`, and `inherit` are less than `3:1` against body text in light mode. In dark mode, all colors except `error` and `textDisabled` are less than `3:1`.<!-- 1.4.1:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum).** <!-- 1.4.3:gap:start -->In light mode, `info` (`3.86:1`), `warning` (`3.11:1`), and `textDisabled` (`2.68:1`) links are less than `4.5:1`.<!-- 1.4.3:gap:end -->

## Success criteria

### 🔍 Manual

#### 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.2:start -->

- A link renders inline, in DOM order with the text around it.
- The order of links in a page is an author decision.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> through a group of links.
2. Compare the focus order with the visual order.

<!-- 1.3.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.2:pass:start -->focus order matches the visual order.<!-- 1.3.2:pass:end -->

#### 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.3:start -->

- A link has visible text, so users identify it by its text, not only by its color or position.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Find product copy that refers to a link.
2. Make sure that it names the link text, not only its color or position.

<!-- 1.3.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.3:pass:start -->no instruction refers to "the blue link" or "the link on the right" alone.<!-- 1.3.3:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.5 Images of Text · AA

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.4.5:start -->

- A link renders real text.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Select the text of each link with the mouse.

<!-- 1.4.5:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.5:pass:start -->the link text is real text, not an image of text.<!-- 1.4.5:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) · AA

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 2.4.11:start -->

- A link is an ordinary focusable element and does not put itself behind other content. Sticky headers and banners can hide it.

**Manual testing steps**

1. In a page with a sticky header, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a link near it.
2. Scroll so that the link is under the header.
3. Press <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd>.
4. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to move focus back to the link.

<!-- 2.4.11:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.11:pass:start -->a part of the focused link stays visible.<!-- 2.4.11:pass:end -->

#### 3.2.4 Consistent Identification · AA

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 3.2.4:start -->

- The name comes from the link text. Consistency across pages is an authoring concern.

**Manual testing steps**

1. List the links that go to the same destination across the product.
2. Compare their text.

<!-- 3.2.4:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 3.2.4:pass:start -->links to the same destination use the same text.<!-- 3.2.4:pass:end -->

### 🔁 Hybrid

#### 1.1.1 Non-text Content · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 1.1.1:start -->

- The accessible name of a link comes from its content. A link that contains only an image needs `alt` text on the image, or an `aria-label` on the link. The author supplies it.
- axe-core `link-name` confirms that each demo link has a name.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Find links that contain only an image or an icon.
2. With a screen reader, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to each of them and listen to the name.

<!-- 1.1.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.1.1:pass:start -->each image link announces its destination or action.<!-- 1.1.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 1.3.1:start -->

- With `href`, the root is an `<a>` with the link role. With `component="button"`, it is a native `<button>`. Unit tests confirm both roles.
- The `variant` prop only sets the typography. The root stays an `<a>`, so `variant="h1"` does not make a heading.
- Without `href`, an `<a>` has no role and is not focusable. Give each link an `href`, or use `component="button"` for an action.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a screen reader, move to each kind of link in use.
2. Listen to the role of each.

<!-- 1.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.1:pass:start -->an `href` link announces "link", and a `component="button"` link announces "button".<!-- 1.3.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.1 Use of Color · A

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `Link.test.js` · axe-core `link-in-text-block` ❌

<!-- 1.4.1:start -->

- With the default `underline="always"`, the underline marks the link, so it does not rely on color. A unit test in a real browser confirms the default underline. The underline uses 40% of the link color, about `1.7:1` against white for `primary`. It is still a non-color cue. On hover, it changes to the full link color.
- With `underline="hover"`, the underline shows only on hover. With `underline="none"`, no underline shows at all. Inside body text, the link must then be at least `3:1` against the body text, and show a non-color cue on hover and focus. `underline="none"` has no hover cue, so it fails unless the author adds another non-color cue.
- With `underline="hover"`, the hover underline and the browser focus outline are the cues. In light mode, `primary`, `error`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, and `textDisabled` pass. In dark mode, only `error` and `textDisabled` pass.
- `textPrimary` and `inherit` have the same color as the body text, so without an underline they always fail the `3:1` check. A custom `color` value needs its own check.
- Unit tests compute each link color against `text.primary`, in light and dark mode, and confirm the failing set.
- Link colors against `text.primary` body text:

  | Color           | Light mode | Dark mode |
  | :-------------- | ---------: | --------: |
  | `primary`       |     3.49:1 |    1.75:1 |
  | `secondary`     |     2.55:1 |    2.39:1 |
  | `error`         |     3.23:1 |    3.68:1 |
  | `info`          |     4.17:1 |    2.30:1 |
  | `success`       |     3.13:1 |    2.36:1 |
  | `warning`       |     5.16:1 |    1.94:1 |
  | `textPrimary`   |     1.00:1 |    1.00:1 |
  | `textSecondary` |     2.80:1 |    1.99:1 |
  | `textDisabled`  |     6.01:1 |    3.52:1 |
  | `inherit`       |     1.00:1 |    1.00:1 |

- axe-core `link-in-text-block` records these failures on the `LinkA11yInTextBlock` fixtures, in light and dark mode. axe rounds some dark-mode values down by 0.01.
- Links outside body text, such as in a navigation list, do not need this cue.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Find a link in body text with `underline="none"`.
2. With a contrast checker, measure the link color against the body text, for each color in use.
3. Switch to dark mode and measure again.
4. Hover over the link and look for a non-color cue.
5. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to the link and look for a non-color cue.
6. Do steps 2 to 5 again with `underline="hover"`.

<!-- 1.4.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.1:pass:start -->the link is at least `3:1` against the body text and shows a non-color cue on hover and on focus. Otherwise, the link fails. `underline="none"` fails unless the author adds another non-color cue.<!-- 1.4.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) · AA

`⚠️ Partially Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `Link.test.js` · axe-core `color-contrast` ❌

<!-- 1.4.3:start -->

- The link text is `palette[color].main`, or `text.primary`, `text.secondary`, or `text.disabled` for the `text*` colors. On hover, only the underline changes.
- Unit tests rate the six palette colors and the three `text*` colors. In light mode, only `info`, `warning`, and `textDisabled` fail. In dark mode, all colors pass. The palette part reads the [palette contrast contract](../../test/contrastContract.ts). axe-core `color-contrast` records the light-mode failure.
- In light mode, `color="textDisabled"` is `2.68:1`. It looks disabled, but the link stays active, so the exemption for inactive components does not apply. The `LinkA11yInTextBlock` fixture includes it.
- Link colors against the page background:

  | Color           | Light mode (`#fff`) | Dark mode (`#121212`) |
  | :-------------- | ------------------: | --------------------: |
  | `primary`       |              4.60:1 |               10.71:1 |
  | `secondary`     |              6.30:1 |                7.84:1 |
  | `error`         |              4.98:1 |                5.09:1 |
  | `info`          |              3.86:1 |                8.13:1 |
  | `success`       |              5.13:1 |                7.92:1 |
  | `warning`       |              3.11:1 |                9.64:1 |
  | `textPrimary`   |             16.07:1 |               18.73:1 |
  | `textSecondary` |              5.74:1 |                9.43:1 |
  | `textDisabled`  |              2.68:1 |                5.32:1 |

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a contrast checker, measure the link color against the background in light mode, for each color in use. The color picker in browser DevTools shows a ratio.
2. Switch to dark mode and measure again.
3. Check any custom theme colors the product uses.

<!-- 1.4.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.3:pass:start -->each link is at least `4.5:1` in light and dark mode. `info`, `warning`, and `textDisabled` fail in light mode.<!-- 1.4.3:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast · AA

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 1.4.11:start -->

- The link text identifies the link, so the underline does not need `3:1`. The underline is the 1.4.1 cue.
- An `href` link keeps the browser focus outline, and the component does not change it.
- A `component="button"` link sets `outline: 0`, and sets `outline: auto` again when it has the `focusVisible` class. The 2.4.7 unit test confirms this in a real browser.
- With `focusVisible: true` on the theme, keyboard focus draws the theme outline ring. It is `primary.main`: `4.60:1` against white, and `10.71:1` against `#121212`.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to an `href` link and to a `component="button"` link.
2. Measure each focus indicator against the colors next to it.

<!-- 1.4.11:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.11:pass:start -->the focus indicator is at least `3:1` against the colors next to it, or it is the unchanged browser outline.<!-- 1.4.11:pass:end -->

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: axe-core `link-name` ✅

<!-- 2.4.4:start -->

- The link text, together with its sentence, must tell the purpose. This is an authoring concern.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Read each link together with the sentence around it.

<!-- 2.4.4:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.4:pass:start -->the purpose of each link is clear, for example "account settings page", not "click here".<!-- 2.4.4:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.6 Headings and Labels · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 2.4.6:start -->

- The link text is the label. Whether it describes the destination is an authoring concern.

**Manual testing steps**

1. List the text of each link.
2. Read each one out of context.

<!-- 2.4.6:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.6:pass:start -->each link text describes its destination or action.<!-- 2.4.6:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.7 Focus Visible · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `Link.test.js` · Playwright

<!-- 2.4.7:start -->

- An `href` link shows the browser focus outline. A `component="button"` link shows `outline: auto` on keyboard focus. A Playwright test confirms that keyboard focus changes how an `href` link looks. A unit test in a real browser confirms the `outline: auto` of a button link.
- With `focusVisible: true` on the theme, the theme outline ring replaces both. Unit tests confirm the ring for both kinds of link.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to an `href` link.
2. Make sure that a focus indicator shows.
3. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a `component="button"` link.
4. Make sure that a focus indicator shows.
5. Set `focusVisible: true` on the theme and do the test again.

<!-- 2.4.7:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.7:pass:start -->each link shows a visible focus indicator on keyboard focus.<!-- 2.4.7:pass:end -->

#### 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `Link.test.js` · axe-core `aria-allowed-attr` ✅, `aria-conditional-attr` ✅, `aria-prohibited-attr` ✅, `aria-valid-attr` ✅, `aria-valid-attr-value` ✅, `button-name` ✅, `link-name` ✅, `nested-interactive` ✅

<!-- 4.1.2:start -->

- An `href` link has the link role, and a `component="button"` link has the button role. The name comes from the content. Unit tests and axe-core `link-name` confirm this.
- Without `href`, the root is an `<a>` with no role, and it is not focusable.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader (NVDA with Chrome, or VoiceOver with Safari).
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to an `href` link.
3. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a `component="button"` link.
4. Listen to the name and role of each.

<!-- 4.1.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 4.1.2:pass:start -->the `href` link announces its text and "link", and the `component="button"` link announces its text and "button".<!-- 4.1.2:pass:end -->

#### 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: axe-core `target-size` ✅

<!-- 2.5.8:start -->

- A link inside a sentence is exempt. A standalone `body2` link, or a `component="button"` link, is 16 to 20 px high. It passes only through the spacing exception, so keep each target center at least 24 px from the next target's center. axe-core `target-size` confirms this on the demos.

<!-- 2.5.8:end -->

## Not applicable

- **1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (AA), 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) (AA).** No audio or video.
- **1.3.4 Orientation (AA).** Sets no orientation lock; a layout concern.
- **1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA).** Collects no information about the user through `autocomplete`.
- **1.4.2 Audio Control (A).** Emits no audio.
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA).** Shows no additional content on hover or focus; a `Tooltip` wrapper would own this.
- **2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (A).** Binds no single-character keyboard shortcut.
- **2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (A).** Sets no time limit.
- **2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A).** No auto-starting moving, blinking, or auto-updating content.
- **2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (A).** Nothing flashes.
- **2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (A), 2.4.2 Page Titled (A), 2.4.5 Multiple Ways (AA).** Page or site structure, not a single component.
- **2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (A), 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (A).** Activates on a simple click; reads no device motion.
- **2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA).** No drag interactions.
- **3.1.1 Language of Page (A), 3.1.2 Language of Parts (AA).** The component emits no `<html lang>` and no text of its own. A foreign-language label is the author's phrase to mark.
- **3.2.2 On Input (A).** <!-- 3.2.2:start -->A link has no setting that the user changes.<!-- 3.2.2:end -->
- **3.2.3 Consistent Navigation (AA).** Covers repeated navigation across a set of pages, not a single component.
- **3.2.6 Consistent Help (A).** Covers consistent placement of help across pages.
- **3.3.1 Error Identification (A), 3.3.3 Error Suggestion (AA), 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) (AA).** Collects and validates no input; these belong to the form or process.
- **3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (A).** <!-- 3.3.2:start -->A link is not a form field.<!-- 3.3.2:end -->
- **3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A).** Captures no previously entered data to repopulate.
- **3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (AA).** No authentication step; the duty falls on the credential fields.
- **4.1.3 Status Messages (AA).** Emits no status messages; state changes are covered by 4.1.2.

## Level AAA

<!-- level-aaa:start -->

- **2.4.9 Link Purpose (Link Only).** The link text alone must tell the purpose. This is an authoring concern. `🚩`
- **3.2.5 Change on Request.** A link with `target="_blank"` gives no warning that it opens a new tab. Say it in the link text. If an `aria-label` gives the warning, it must contain the visible text (2.5.3). `🚩`
- **1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced), 7:1.** In light mode, all six palette colors are less than 7:1. In dark mode, `error` is `5.09:1`. `🚩`

<!-- level-aaa:end -->

## Scope and test environment

- **Standard.** WCAG 2.2, Level A and AA.
- **Component version.** `@mui/material` 10.0.0-alpha.0.

<!-- scope:start -->

- **Scope.** The Link component in isolation, rendered through its documented API, in light and dark mode.
- **Automated.** axe-core in the Playwright test harness, on the Link demos and fixtures in [`links.a11y.json`](../../../../docs/data/material/components/links/links.a11y.json). Interaction and contrast tests are in `Link.test.js`.
- **Assistive-technology review.** Not done yet. The flagged criteria come from a review of the source. A review with NVDA, JAWS, and VoiceOver must still confirm them.

<!-- scope:end -->
